concepts.label: curl() call (Eventing handler outbound HTTP)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the built-in curl() JS function that lets an Eventing handler call out to an external REST endpoint; distinct from, but dependent on, the already-promoted eventing:binding concept. A sibling batch extracting eventing-curl-spec.md directly is likely minting the canonical id for this same mechanism - this id is chosen to be a plausible match for reconciliation.

relations.subject: eventing:curl-call
relations.evidence: Needs a Binding of type URL Alias (as documented in the Scriptlet).

relations.subject: cloud/eventing/eventing-handler-curl-get
relations.evidence: For a more complete example using this public REST endpoint (or to make your own service), refer to [External REST via cURL GET](eventing-examples-rest-via-curl-get.md).

notable_absence.finding: This page confirms the batch hypothesis's speculation directly: calling out to an external HTTP service from a handler is gated by a 'URL Alias' Binding (a sub-type of the already-known eventing:binding concept), which acts as the access-control/allow-list mechanism - a handler can only curl() a URL that has a pre-configured URL Alias binding pointing at it, and that binding's base URL constrains what curl() can reach. The settings comment block's binding row also carries a 'misc.' column value of 'no auth', implying other auth modes exist for URL Alias bindings, but none are named or explained on this page - only inferable from the column's existence.
